metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
vague/subjective terms present: better
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Select ONE candidate approach (or state the decision criteria and a default) so the ticket is executable without a clarifying round-trip.
evidence: 'Candidate approaches (choose ONE during planning; none is pre-selected here)'
The three options differ in scope: cache config, 25-call-site reimplementation, and an upstream PR + pin bump
findings.finding: The plan defers the core design decision ('choose ONE during planning; none is pre-selected here') across three materially different approaches with very different file impacts (an actions/cache config vs. rewriting 25 call sites / a composite action vs. upstreaming a PR). An executing agent cannot proceed without settling which approach to build.
scenarios: An implementer picks up the ticket and must stop to decide which of three approaches to build before any work can start.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit to one approach (e.g. approach 1, actions/cache keyed on the pinned version, as the lowest-blast-radius option) and record the rejected alternatives as considered-and-declined.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the AC #1 liveness anchor approach-dependent (name the action-specific anchor when setup-uv is retained, and specify an equivalent approach-2/3 liveness anchor such as a `uv --version` echo of the pinned value) so the criterion is provable under whichever approach is chosen.
evidence: AC: 'a real CI log ... contains the liveness anchor `Successfully installed uv version <pinned>`'
Approach 2: 'Install uv without the action (direct download from releases.astral.sh ...)' — the setup-uv success message would not be printed
findings.finding: AC #1's mandated liveness anchor 'Successfully installed uv version <pinned>' is a string emitted by the astral-sh/setup-uv action, but candidate approach 2 (install uv directly without the action) and approach 3 (upstream change) either remove or alter the action that prints it. Under approach 2 that exact anchor line will never appear, making the acceptance criterion unsatisfiable and contradicting the candidate-approach section.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria line 1 vs. Candidate approaches bullet 2
scenarios: Approach 2 is chosen; the log shows a direct download succeeding but no 'Successfully installed uv version' line, so AC #1 fails despite a correct fix.
findings.suggested_fix: State per-approach liveness anchors, e.g. 'Successfully installed uv version <pinned>' for the action-based approaches and an explicit `uv --version` == <pinned> echo for the direct-download approach.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] For the chosen approach, state the disposition on the non-hit arm (e.g. actions/cache MISS): whether CI degrades back to the manifest fetch (reintroducing the bug) or fails/warns, so a cold/evicted cache cannot silently reintroduce the raw.githubusercontent.com fetch.
evidence: 'so tryGetFromToolCache hits and downloadVersion never runs'
Root cause: 'on a miss it calls downloadVersion, whose first statement is ... getArtifact(...) // the manifest fetch'
A cache miss (cold cache, evicted entry, key change) re-enters the exact code path the plan removes — the fallback arm's disposition is unstated.
findings.finding: For the actions/cache approach (candidate 1), the plan does not state what disposition surfaces on a cache MISS. On a miss, tryGetFromToolCache falls through to downloadVersion, which is exactly the manifest fetch the plan is eliminating — so a cache miss silently reintroduces the raw.githubusercontent.com fetch (masking the fix) rather than failing loudly. The disposition of the miss arm should be stated: does CI hard-fail, or degrade back to the manifest fetch?
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the chosen approach: state that a cache miss (or absence of the restored binary) is surfaced — e.g. the install step fails or emits a warning — rather than silently falling through to downloadVersion's manifest fetch; AC1's 'zero occurrences of Fetching manifest data' should be asserted on a cache-miss run as well as a cache-hit run.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] If actions/cache is chosen, define the cache lifecycle: key (pinned version), who populates it and when (cold-start on pin bump), and that eviction/staleness is bounded by the version key.
evidence: 'Restore the uv binary into the runner tool cache with actions/cache keyed on the pinned version'
The plan states the key but not the create/populate step nor the cold-start behavior on a pin bump.
findings.finding: If the actions/cache approach is chosen, the plan does not specify the cache lifecycle: the cache key ('keyed on the pinned version'), who populates it initially (first run after a pin bump is a cold miss), and its retire/eviction behavior. A version-keyed cache retires naturally on pin bump, but the cold-start (first run at a new pin) is a guaranteed miss that must still install correctly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Back the 'committed local manifest does not help' exclusion with a verifiable reference (a quote from the pinned action's src pointing to fetch() usage, or the action's manifest-file input docs), since fetchManifestResponse is not present in this repo and cannot be resolved locally.
evidence: Plan: 'fetchManifestResponse uses Node fetch(), which rejects file: URLs, and manifest-file is documented as a URL.'
search_files 'fetchManifestResponse' -> (no matches) in repo
src/ contains only rebar/ (list_directory) — the cited src/download/download-version.ts and src/setup-uv.ts are the vendored-action's files, not in this repo
This claim excludes a mitigation (SCOPE-EXCLUSION G-4 shape): 'A committed local manifest does not help'
findings.finding: The Root Cause claim that a committed local manifest cannot help — 'fetchManifestResponse uses Node fetch(), which rejects file: URLs, and manifest-file is documented as a URL' — is an assertion about third-party astral-sh/setup-uv internals that is not present in this repo (src/ contains only rebar/), is not resolvable via resolve_symbol (it is TypeScript action source, not an importable Python symbol), and is not backed by a cited prerequisite ticket. It is load-bearing because it is used to exclude the committed-local-manifest mitigation. Fail-closed: unverifiable.
scenarios: If fetch() in the pinned action version actually tolerates file: URLs, or manifest-file accepts a local path, the committed-manifest mitigation is viable and was wrongly excluded
findings.suggested_fix: Pin the exact action SHA and quote the relevant lines of its fetch-manifest-file.ts / action.yml input docs at that SHA, or note that this exclusion is unverifiable from the repo and treat the committed-manifest approach as open.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify KNOWN_CHECKSUMS exists in the pinned astral-sh/setup-uv source and contains the pinned uv version's checksum (cite the file+line at the pinned SHA), or mark approach 3's premise as unverified.
evidence: Plan: 'skips getArtifact when the version is exact and the checksum is already in KNOWN_CHECKSUMS'
search_files 'KNOWN_CHECKSUMS' -> (no matches) in repo
findings.finding: Candidate approach 3 rests on 'the checksum is already in KNOWN_CHECKSUMS', an assertion about the third-party action's source that is not in this repo (search returns no matches), not resolvable via resolve_symbol, and not backed by a cited prerequisite. Fail-closed: unverifiable.
scenarios: If KNOWN_CHECKSUMS does not contain the pinned uv version's checksum (or does not exist under that name at the pinned SHA), the proposed upstream skip would still need a network fetch and the approach's premise fails

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] For approach 1 (actions/cache), enumerate the per-call-site edit surface (cache step at each of the ~25 setup-uv call sites, or a single shared composite action) as approach 2 already does.
evidence: Approach 2 names its blast radius: 'reimplemented at 25 call sites or in one composite action'
Approach 1 states only 'Restore the uv binary into the runner tool cache with actions/cache' with no edit-surface count
Repo has ~25 'astral-sh/setup-uv@...' uses: lines across test.yml, release.yml, external-integration.yml, _build-and-test.yml, _mutation.yml, gerrit-verify.yaml, and others
findings.finding: Approach 1 (actions/cache keyed on the pinned version so tryGetFromToolCache hits) would require inserting a cache/restore step at each of the ~25 setup-uv call sites across .github/workflows/, but unlike approach 2 the plan does not enumerate this per-call-site edit surface.
scenarios: When approach 1 is selected during planning, the author discovers the cache step must be added to every workflow, not one place, unless a composite action is introduced

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] For candidate 1, establish (from setup-uv's source at the pinned SHA) that a runner-tool-cache entry restored by actions/cache is what tryGetFromToolCache reads AND that getArtifact is genuinely skipped on that hit, and explain why the enable-cache: true already present at all 25 sites does not already warm this path — or drop the candidate.
evidence: search_files across .github/workflows shows `enable-cache: true` on every setup-uv step (test.yml:107, release.yml:117, _build-and-test.yml:65, external-integration.yml:113…, all 25 sites)
Plan text: 'Restore the uv binary into the runner tool cache with actions/cache keyed on the pinned version, so tryGetFromToolCache hits and downloadVersion never runs'

Root cause (from 56b7 comment, cited in this plan): getArtifact is reached on a tool-cache MISS; if setup-uv's own enable-cache already populated the tool cache the fetch would not recur — so the observed persistent fetch implies enable-cache does NOT warm the path tryGetFromToolCache checks, which approach 1 depends on
findings.finding: Approach 1 (bolt-on actions/cache to seed the tool cache so tryGetFromToolCache hits) does not reckon with the fact that all 25 setup-uv call sites ALREADY set enable-cache: true, nor establish that setup-uv reads/writes the same tool-cache location actions/cache would restore; the mechanism may not achieve the goal.
findings.location: Candidate approaches — first bullet (actions/cache tool-cache seeding)
scenarios: Implementer adds actions/cache keyed on 0.12.7, but setup-uv still calls getArtifact because the action does not consult that restored path on cache hit — the fetch (and the ##[error]fetch failed failure mode) survives, and AC1's zero-'Fetching manifest data' assertion fails after the work is done
findings.suggested_fix: In the candidate-1 bullet, cite the setup-uv code path from tryGetFromToolCache through the tool-cache directory it probes, show it matches what actions/cache would restore, and reconcile it with the existing enable-cache: true; if setup-uv's own cache inputs can seed that path, prefer them over a parallel actions/cache step.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Before committing approach 1, verify (against setup-uv's downloadVersion/tryGetFromToolCache source at the pinned SHA) the exact tool-cache directory, tool name, version, and arch/platform key that produces a HIT, and confirm actions/cache can restore into that path — or route this to a SPIKE that proves one cached job logs zero 'Fetching manifest data'.
evidence: Plan: 'Restore the uv binary into the runner tool cache with actions/cache keyed on the pinned version, so tryGetFromToolCache hits and downloadVersion never runs.'
Plan verifies the miss: 'A GitHub-hosted runner starts each job with an empty uv tool cache, so the miss is guaranteed' — but not the hit.

setup-uv is an external action, not vendored in this repo; the tool-cache path/key contract is not readable via repo-scoped tools — Partially-verified (the resolver flow is described but the cache-hit surface is unconfirmed).
findings.finding: Candidate approach 1 (actions/cache + tryGetFromToolCache) depends on the UNVERIFIED capability that a cache-restored uv binary produces a tryGetFromToolCache HIT that skips downloadVersion/getArtifact. The plan verifies only the MISS path ('empty uv tool cache ... miss is guaranteed'); it does not verify that actions/cache can restore into the exact tool-cache directory/arch/platform key layout that tryGetFromToolCache queries, which is the whole mechanism of the fix.
scenarios: Approach 1 is chosen; actions/cache restores the tar into a path tryGetFromToolCache does not consult (wrong tool name / version-dir / arch layout), the lookup still misses, downloadVersion runs, and getArtifact fetches the manifest anyway — the fix ships without removing the fetch.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Before choosing approach 3, verify against astral-sh/setup-uv source at a named SHA that KNOWN_CHECKSUMS exists, is populated for the pinned uv version on every CI target platform/arch, and that getArtifact's return can be fully satisfied from it — record MATCH/MISMATCH with the file:line.
evidence: Plan: 'skips getArtifact when the version is exact and the checksum is already in KNOWN_CHECKSUMS'.
KNOWN_CHECKSUMS is named as an existing upstream symbol but no source location / SHA is cited, unlike the getArtifact citation ('src/download/download-version.ts:42'). Unverified external capability.
findings.finding: Candidate approach 3 asserts the setup-uv symbol KNOWN_CHECKSUMS exists and that getArtifact can be skipped when the checksum is already present — an external-repo internal capability that is unverified in the plan. If KNOWN_CHECKSUMS is not populated for the pinned version/platform, or getArtifact returns more than the URL+sha the plan assumes, the upstream change does not achieve the skip.
scenarios: Approach 3 is chosen and an upstream PR is opened assuming KNOWN_CHECKSUMS covers the pinned uv version on every target platform; if it does not (or is only a fallback consulted after the manifest), the change does not remove the fetch and the pin-bump step buys nothing.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Cite the setup-uv source (fetchManifestResponse, file:line at a named SHA) and the manifest-file input documentation (versioned URL) that together establish local/file: manifests are unsupported — or drop the categorical exclusion.
evidence: Plan: 'A committed local manifest does not help: fetchManifestResponse uses Node fetch(), which rejects file: URLs, and manifest-file is documented as a URL.'
Unlike the getArtifact claim, neither the fetch()/file: behavior nor the manifest-file documentation is cited to a file/line or a doc URL at a pinned version — Unverified.
findings.finding: The plan rules out a committed local manifest on two asserted external-capability claims — 'fetchManifestResponse uses Node fetch(), which rejects file: URLs' and 'manifest-file is documented as a URL' — without a cited source/SHA for either. This exclusion is load-bearing (it removes an otherwise-cheap zero-network option), so an unverified claim here could discard a viable approach.
scenarios: A reviewer or the author later finds that manifest-file (or a newer setup-uv input) does accept a local path, meaning the committed-manifest option was discarded on an unverified premise and a cheaper fix was overlooked.

findings.checklist_item: If approach 1 (actions/cache) is selected, state how the integrity of the uv binary restored from the GitHub cache is verified before execution (e.g. the cache is seeded only from a checksum-verified download, or the restored binary is sha256-checked against the pin), so the fix does not swap a checksummed install for an unverified one.
evidence: Approach 1: 'Restore the uv binary into the runner tool cache with actions/cache keyed on the pinned version ... Trades a raw.githubusercontent.com dependency for a GitHub-cache-service dependency'
AC3 requires naming the 'residual network dependency' but not the integrity/checksum of the restored artifact
Approach 2 by contrast pins 'a committed sha256'; the docs precedent (docs/jira-sync-setup.md:125-128) pins acli version + sha256
test.yml:105-107 shows setup-uv used with enable-cache:true across privileged jobs; a cache entry executes as the toolchain
findings.finding: Under approach 1 (actions/cache keyed on the pinned uv version), the plan does not state how the integrity of the uv binary restored from the GitHub cache is verified before it is executed. The other two approaches name an integrity control (committed sha256 / KNOWN_CHECKSUMS); approach 1 names only the residual network dependency, not the integrity posture of the cached executable, even though that binary runs as the toolchain across ~25 call sites, some holding contents:write / actions:write and secrets.
findings.location: Candidate approaches (approach 1) and Acceptance Criteria line 3
scenarios: A poisoned or corrupted GitHub cache entry for the pinned uv version is restored and executed with a job's contents:write/actions:write token and secrets, with no checksum gate to catch it
